gemini.rationale: The drawn accession is a charter/bylaw correction (8-K Item 5.03) that merely restates a defined term, not a transaction crossing an ownership boundary. Therefore, no assets, processes, or people transferred, resulting in no structural gaps at closing.

grok.rationale: The slice shows the customer-facing portfolio (296 industrial buildings / ~57.2M sq ft, including 2013 acquisitions) crossed into consolidated company ownership while property-level operating processes remained outside with Dividend Capital Property Management LLC and day-to-day operating/acquisition activities remained with the external Advisor, producing a documented T4-vs-T5 structural mismatch at closing (gap_45=1). T5 and T6 did not separate: the company had 'no employees,' and both the processes and the key personnel who run them sat together with the Advisor and related-party Property Manager, so gap_56=0; the Advisory Agreement and property-management fee arrangements contractually allocated that shared external substrate (gap_mitigated=yes).

openai.rationale: The customer-facing assets crossed the ownership boundary through serial acquisitions of 75 buildings and the partner’s Fund I equity interest, becoming part of the consolidated industrial portfolio, while property management, leasing, and day-to-day operations remained with the external Advisor and related-party Property Manager rather than transferring with those assets [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-058795, 10-K FY2013]. This product-versus-process separation establishes gap_45, but it was contractually absorbed through the Advisory Agreement and property-management arrangements. Gap_56 is zero because the external operational processes remained aligned with the external personnel who performed them; the company had no employees and relied on the Advisor’s key personnel to conduct those activities [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-058795, 10-K FY2013].
